name: Audio output device selection (selectAudioOutput)
plain: Lets a site pick which speaker or headphones play audio.
meaning: Lets a site list and choose speakers. The chooser shows device names only after a pick, because output names can reveal paired Bluetooth gear and hardware.

access.prompt_ui: Browser chooser lists output devices; the site receives the chosen deviceId only.
access.persistence: Per origin and device after a pick
access.revocation: Site settings; revoke by clearing site data
steps: Site gets a MediaDeviceInfo and calls setSinkId()

edge.note: BCD lists no support; agent research says otherwise

chrome_android.note: BCD lists no support; agent research says otherwise

limits.headline: Can send sound to the speaker or headphones you pick
limits.user_action: You click Choose speaker in a call or music page and pick a device from the list
can: Play audio through the output device you choose
Remember which output device you picked
Switch between speakers and headphones during a call
cannot: Pick a device for you without the browser chooser
See devices you did not choose in the list
Hear sound or record anything, since this only controls where audio plays
Work in Samsung Internet; Safari and iPhone browsers support only part of it
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Firefox support it fully. Safari and iPhone browsers support only part of it.

story.what_it_is: Lets a site choose which speaker or headphones plays its sound, after you pick one.

marketing.name: selectAudioOutput
marketing.pitch: Developer docs say a page can ask the person to choose an audio output device, and then play sound there.

story.for_you: A small picker lists your speakers and headphones, and you choose one. After that, the site plays sound to that device, for example your headset and not the laptop speakers.
story.for_makers: In calls and games, sending voices to a headset and game sound to a speaker makes a nicer product, with no need to dig through system settings. The picker hides the device names until you choose, since names like a car stereo or earbuds can reveal your life.

use_cases.example: In a call, you pick your headset for the voice of others, and your laptop speaker for the ringing sound.
A browser game sends the voice chat to your headset and the game music to your room speakers.
A web music tool lets a DJ send the cue track to headphones while the crowd hears the main mix.
A contact center web phone sends the customer voice to a headset, and keeps the ring on the desk speaker.
A language class page sends a teacher voice to headphones, so a student in a shared room is not heard by others.
A person using a hearing loop or special headset chooses it as the output for a call.

risks: Sound can go to a device you forgot about

technical_bounds: Output labels hidden until a pick

abuse: Learning a person's connected audio hardware

history.change: Speaker selection support on iOS and iPadOS (version unconfirmed)
